text: when we were at the phone-device stage, it irked me that i couldn't just pull in the shell and run it on that device.

That's the same test, failing for the shell. Today the shell only works when a node serves it: every call it makes goes to '/api/spirit' on the node that served the page (kernel.js:647). So the interface is welded to the compute behind it, and a phone can't just run it against your home node. Orthogonal would be: the shell is a page anywhere, and the node it talks to is a setting, reached through the same interface routing we discussed (the device as a window). It belongs to the 'route a complete node interface' goal, and it may be the clearest first use of it.

wsl-claude: that one has a single cause in the tree, and it's the same seam as tonight's G1.3. The shell's one mouth onto the node, spirit.core.ask, is a fetch to the RELATIVE address '/api/spirit' (kernel.js:647). So the shell can only ever talk to the node that served its page. It's welded to one node by an address it never chose. On a phone, the page came from somewhere else, so there's no node on the other end of that relative path.
Make ask's target a parameter (the local door by default, or a given address: a process's callback, or your home node reached through the relay as a device) and three things fall out of one change: processes can ask (G1.3), the shell runs on a phone as a window onto home, and a laptop on the road is the same case. Human interface and node, separated at exactly one line.

wsl-claude: the CONTROL half of that is already there. A puppet obeys your signed commands for the groups it carries, so carrying 'jobs' lets your node start a tagging batch on another box (jobs.create), and carrying 'fs' lets it read and write there. The DATA half isn't, and it's the one wall to name now: every message across the relay is capped at 16 KB of plaintext (limits.js PLAINTEXT_MAX = 16384). A photo to tag, or a file to store elsewhere, doesn't fit in one, and there's no bulk channel. So distributed compute works today when the data is already where the work runs (a box tagging its own media); moving the data itself needs a way to stream large content between your nodes, in pieces or directly. That's the piece to design before 'Google, but p2p'.
